'''Annie Sugier''' (born 21 February 1942) is a French [[Nuclear physics|nuclear physicist]] and [[Feminism|feminist activist]]. She came to prominence in 1989 as the first woman to be promoted to a directorship at France's [[French Alternative Energies and Atomic Energy Commission|"Alternative Energies and Atomic Energy Commission" (''"Commissariat à l'énergie atomique et aux énergies alternatives"'' / CEA)]]. The focus of her responsibilities at the CEA was on the dismantling of nuclear installations.

Sugier has served for many years as president of the "Ligue du droit international des femmes" (''"International Women's Rights League"'')<!---In view of her age, at the time of producing this adaptation/translation from the entry in wiki-fr, I frequently cartch myself wondering whether she is STILL president of the LIDF.   She is.  At least, that is how she is described at the head of her column in Le Monde on 9 January 2021: "Dans une tribune au « Monde », la présidente de la Ligue du droit international des femmes, Annie Sugier, reproche notamment à la militante antiraciste de justifier les comportements des garçons issus de l’immigration par leur victimisation supposée..."--->, founded in 1983 by her friend and mentor, [[Simone de Beauvoir]].<ref name="ASselonOM">{{cite web|title=Répertoire numérique détaillé .... Zone du contexte .... Notice biographique: Annie Sugier |work=Centre des Archives du Féminisme .... Fonds Annie Sugier|author1=Olivia Même (compilation) |author2=France Chabod (direction) |publisher=Bibliothèque universitaire d'Angers |date=2016|url=https://bu.univ-angers.fr/sites/default/files/inventaire_sugier.pdf|access-date=8 January 2021}}</ref><ref name="ASselonGB">{{cite web|title=Venue d'Annie Sugier|date=October 2018 |publisher= Observatoire Vendéen de la Laïcité "Georges Clémenceau" |work=Communiqué de presse envoyé à l’occasion de la venue de Annie Sugier en Vendée|url= http://www.ovlgc.org/fr/venue-de-annie-sugier/ |author= Gilles Bourmaud (Président) |access-date= 28 January 2021}}</ref><ref name="ASselonSH">{{cite web|title=Vendée: Annie Sugier, présidente de la Ligue du droit international des femmes à La Roche le 27 octobre |work=Annie Sugier, physicienne et féministe de renom, tiendra une conférence samedi 27 octobre à La Roche-sur-Yon. |author= Stéphanie Hourdeau |date=15 October 2018 |url= https://actu.fr/pays-de-la-loire/la-roche-sur-yon_85191/vendee-annie-sugier-presidente-la-ligue-droit-international-femmes-la-roche-27-octobre_19064217.html |publisher= [[:fr:Actu.fr|actu.fr]]: Le Journal du pays Yonnais |access-date=28 January 2021}}</ref><ref name="LDIFselonSB">{{cite web |title= Trente ans de combats avec la Ligue du droit international des femmes |url= https://information.tv5monde.com/terriennes/trente-ans-de-combats-avec-la-ligue-du-droit-international-des-femmes-3342 |date=28 August 2014 |author=Sylvie Braibant |work= Terriennes .... Féminismes: L'actualité de la condition des femmes dans le monde |publisher=[[TV5Monde|TV5 Monde]] |access-date= 28 January 2021}}</ref><ref name="ASTribune09jan2021">{{cite web |author=Annie Sugier |date=9 January 2021 |title=Lettre à Assa Traoré : "La lutte contre le racisme ne doit pas occulter la lutte contre les violences faites aux femmes" |url=https://www.lemonde.fr/idees/article/2021/01/09/lettre-a-assa-traore-la-lutte-contre-le-racisme-ne-doit-pas-occulter-la-lutte-contre-les-violences-faites-aux-femmes_6065683_3232.html |work=Tribune: Dans une tribune au « Monde », la présidente de la Ligue du droit international des femmes, Annie Sugier, reproche notamment à la militante antiraciste de justifier les comportements des garçons issus de l’immigration par leur victimisation supposée}}</ref>

== Biography ==
=== Professional ===
'''Annie Sugier''' was born in [[Courcelles-lès-Lens]], a small town a short distance to the south of [[Lille]] in the extreme north of [[France]]. At that time Courcelles was still dominated by its coal mine.<ref name=ASselonwhoswho>{{cite web |url=https://www.whoswho.fr/bio/annie-sugier_60250 |title=Annie Sugier |work=Ingénieure, Présidente d'association féministe  |publisher=Who's Who in France (au Who's Who depuis 2007) |access-date=28 January 2021}}</ref>   Her father worked as a chemical engineer:  her mother was a nurse.<ref name=ASselonAF>{{cite web |title=Annie Sugier |work=Scientifique et militante féministe française |publisher=Éditions des femmes-Antoinette Fouque (Le Dictionnaire universel des Créatrices), Paris |url= https://www.dictionnaire-creatrices.com/fiche-annie-sugier |access-date=28 January 2021}}</ref> She received her primary schooling in [[Argentina]] and [[Brazil]], returning for her secondary schooling to [[Europe]] where she attended schools in [[Spain]] and [[France]].<ref name=ASprovenanceselonMD>{{cite web |title=Présentation d'Annie Sugier |url=http://www.ovlgc.org/fr/presentation-dannie-sugier-par-madeleine-david-vice-presidente-de-lovlgc/ |author=Madeleine David |date=2 November 2018 |publisher=Observatoire Vendéen de la Laïcité "Georges Clémenceau" |access-date=28 January 2021}}</ref> She received degrees in [[Physics]] and [[Chemistry]] at the [[Paris-Saclay Faculty of Sciences|"Faculté des sciences d'Orsay"]], part of the [[Paris-Saclay University]].<ref name=ASselonSénat>{{cite web|url=http://www.senat.fr/opecst/biographies_conseil_scientifique/sugier_annie.pdf|title=Annie Sugier|work=Carrière et activités|publisher=Sénat (Office parlementaire d'évaluation des choix scientifiques et technologiques), Paris|access-date=28 January 2021}}</ref>

Sugier then embarked on a career as an industrial chemist, specialising in the reprocessing of [[radioactive waste]], employed as an engineer with the [[French Alternative Energies and Atomic Energy Commission|CEA]] (in a division subsequently reconfigured, and now part of [[Areva|Areva S.A.]]). She was then appointed to head up the research programmes on the treatment and care of [[radioactive waste]]. In 1989 she took charge of the [[French Alternative Energies and Atomic Energy Commission|CEA]] department responsible for the dismantling of nuclear installations, becoming the CEA's first female director.<ref name="ASselonL-EJ">{{cite web |title=Société française de radioprotection Annie Sugier |work= Les Echos |url= https://www.lesechos.fr/1995/07/societe-francaise-de-radioprotection-annie-sugier-861539 |publisher=[[Les Echos (France)|Les Échos]], [[Paris]]|date=3 July 1995|access-date=28 January 2021}}</ref> In 1992, she oversaw the integration of the [[:fr:Institut de protection et de sûreté nucléaire|"Institute for Nuclear Protection and Safety"]] (which at that time was an institute under the umbrella  of the [[French Alternative Energies and Atomic Energy Commission|CEA]], and which later, in 2002, was rebranded and relaunched as the now autonomous [[Institut de radioprotection et de sûreté nucléaire|"Radioprotection and Nuclear Safety Institute" (''"Institut de radioprotection et de sûreté nucléaire"'' / IRSN)]].   She held the post of "directrice déléguée à la radioprotection" (''loosely, "under-director for radioprotection"'').<ref name="ASselonSénat" />   This meant that she was responsible for evaluating the scientific data needed for setting radioprotection standards.<ref name="ASselonCNDP2005">{{cite web |title=Débat public EPR "Tête de série" Caen |url=https://cpdp.debatpublic.fr/cpdp-epr/docs/pdf/verbatims/cr-caen-20051123.pdf |date=23 November 2005 |work=compte-rendu |publisher=[[:fr:Commission nationale du débat public|Commission nationale du débat public]], [[Paris]] |access-date=28 January 2021}}</ref>   She also held an advisory role on radioprotection in support of the [[Institut de radioprotection et de sûreté nucléaire|IRSN]] [[:fr:Jacques Repussard|director general]].<ref name="ASselonSénat" />

Recognised internationally for her radioprotection expertise, she has held a series of specialist posts connected with the [[European Commission]] under the auspices of the [[European Atomic Energy Community|"Euratom]] Article 31 experts", as an expert member of the [[International Atomic Energy Agency|IAEA]] radioprotection committee, and as an expert member of the technical committee at the [[International Commission on Radiological Protection|ICRP]].<ref name="ICRPsansdate">{{cite web |url=https://www.icrp.org/docs/ICRP_approves_new_fundamental_Recommendations.pdf|title=CRP approves new fundamental Recommendations on radiological protection |access-date=29 January 2021}}</ref><ref>{{cite book |url=https://books.google.com/books?id=tv9uouwihFIC&pg=PA351 |title=Nuclear Safety |publisher=Technical Information Center of the U.S. Department of Energy |year=1994 |page=351}}</ref>   Further recognition was reflected in her appointment by Health and Environment Ministers to presidency, in 1997, of the " Groupe Radioécologie Nord-Cotentin" (GRNC).   The creation of this interdisciplinary expert group was a first in the world of nuclear sciences.   It came in response to scientific disagreement triggered by an epidemiological study postulating a connection between emissions from the [[La Hague site|La Hague]] [[Nuclear reprocessing|reprocessing plant]] and a heightened incidence of [[Leukaemia]] among young people in the surrounding neighbourhood.   Numerous articles by specialists, sociologist and journalists covering related issues of risk management followed.<ref name="NoCoEtu">{{cite journal |title=Comparison Between Radiological and Chemical Health Risks Assessments: The Nord-Cotentin Study |journal= Human and Ecological Risk Assessment|year=2005 |url= https://www.tandfonline.com/doi/abs/10.1080/10807030590949726 |volume=11/3 |author1=Catherine Mercat-Rommens |author2=Didier Louvat |author3=Céline Duffa |author4= Annie Sugier  |issue= 3 |pages= 627–644 |publisher=Taylor Francis online |doi= 10.1080/10807030590949726 |bibcode= 2005HERA...11..627M|s2cid= 72692529 |access-date=29 January 2021|url-access=subscription }}</ref><ref name="Nord-Cotentin">{{cite journal |url= https://inis.iaea.org/search/search.aspx?orig_q=RN:39087077 |title=Le Groupe radioécologie Nord-Cotentin / The North Cotentin radioecology group .... abstract |author1=Miserey, Y. |author2= Pellegrini, P |journal=Éditions la Documentation Française |location=Paris, France |date=2007 |publisher= International Atomic Energy Agency (IAEA), Wien |access-date= 29 January 2021}}</ref>   Applying the same model, Sugier then accepted a request by Ministers of Health, Economics and Industry to set up a second interdisciplinary expert group to investigate [[:fr:Industrie minière en Limousin|the old]] [[Uranium]] [[Uranium mining|mines in]] [[Limousin]] (in south-central France), in order to assess their environmental impact.<ref name="ancmindiurLim">{{cite web|title=Premier rapport du groupe d'expertise pluraliste sur les anciennes mines d'uranium du Limousin|date=5 February 2007|work=Communiques et dossiers de presse ... les ministres en charge de l’environnement, de la santé et de l’industrie, ont annoncé ...|url=https://www.irsn.fr/FR/Actualites_presse/Communiques_et_dossiers_de_presse/Pages/rapport_gep_mines_uranium_limousin.aspx|publisher=[[Institut de radioprotection et de sûreté nucléaire]], [[Fontenay-aux-Roses]]|access-date=29 January 2021}}</ref>

Within the still resolutely male-dominated [[Ottawa]]-based [[International Commission on Radiological Protection|"International Commission on Radiological Protection" (ICRP)]] she became the first woman to be entrusted with the presidency of one of the technical committees:  Committee 4, responsible for regulatory system applications.<ref name=CoRe04dec07>{{cite web |title=Travaux engagés par la CIPR pour la mise en œuvre de ses recommandations (Annie Sugier, IRSN) |url=https://www.irsn.fr/GT-CIPR/Documents/04-12-2007/GT-CIPR_04-12-2007_CR.pdf |work=compte-rendu de la reunion du GT-CIPR IRSN 4 décembre 2007|date=29 January 2008|publisher=[[Institut de radioprotection et de sûreté nucléaire|IRSN)]], [[Fontenay-aux-Roses]]|access-date=29 January 2021}}</ref>   In this context Sugier took a leading role in producing a new set of [[International Commission on Radiological Protection|ICRP]] recommendations (Publication 60}<ref name= ICRP2006recommendations>{{cite web |title=ICRP 2006 recommendations GT CIPR |date=7 December 2006 |author=Annie Sugier |url= https://www.irsn.fr/GT-CIPR/Documents/07-12-2006/GT-CIPR_07-12-2006_1-Sugier.pdf |work=overview & process-flow|publisher=[[Institut de radioprotection et de sûreté nucléaire|IRSN)]], [[Fontenay-aux-Roses]] |access-date=29 January 2021}}</ref> and in the drafting of other more specialist publications on emergencies management and land contamination.

She served two terms as a member of the "Scientific Council" at the [[:fr:Office parlementaire d'évaluation des choix scientifiques et technologiques|French parliamentary office for evaluation of scientific and technological choices]], of the "Scientific Council" for the [[:fr:Bassin Seine-Normandie|Seine-Normandie region]] and of the influential [[Mines ParisTech|National Mines Academy]].<ref name=ConScoMem>{{cite web |title=Conseil scientifique - Désignation des membres |url= http://www.senat.fr/commission/offices/office031117.html |date=12 November 2003 |publisher=Sénat (Office parlementaire d'évaluation des choix scientifiques et technologiques), Paris |access-date= 29 January 2021}}</ref><ref name=MemCoSci>{{cite web|title=Annie Sigier - Carrière et activités|publisher= Assemblée nationale|work=Membres Co-scientifiques |url=https://www.assemblee-nationale.fr/connaissance/membres%20consscientif/Sugier%20Annie.pdf |access-date=29 January 2021}}</ref>   She also served two terms as president of the "Scientific Council" at the [[:fr:Centre d'étude sur l'évaluation de la protection dans le domaine nucléaire|"Centre d'étude sur l'évaluation de la protection dans le domaine nucléaire" (study centre for evaluation of nuclear protection)]] at [[Fontenay-aux-Roses]].<ref name=CEPNPresi>{{cite web |url=https://www.cepn.asso.fr/en/presentation/historical.html|title=... Successive Presidents of the Association|work=CEPN - Historical|publisher=Centre d’étude sur l’Evaluation de la Protection dans le domaine Nucléaire |access-date=29 January 2021}}</ref>

=== Activist ===
During the 1970s Annie Sugier engaged with the [[Mouvement de libération des femmes|women's liberation movement]].  In 1974/75 she was a co-founder of the "Ligue du droit des femmes" (''"Women's rights league"''), together with [[Simone de Beauvoir]], [[Vicky Colombet]], [[:fr:Anne Zelensky|Anne Zelensky]] and [[Annie Cohen]].<ref name=ASselonOM/><ref>{{Cite journal |last= Zelensky |first=Anne |date=2017-03-12|title=Une lignée de rébellion |url=http://www.cairn.info/resume.php?ID_ARTICLE=LTM_647_0256 |journal=Les Temps Modernes |issue=647–648 |pages=256–264 |issn=0040-3075}}</ref>   In 1978, with backing from [[Simone Veil]], Sugier opened the refuge for battered women at [[Clichy, Hauts-de-Seine|Clichy]].<ref name=ASselonOM/>

The longstanding president of the  "International Women's Rights League" (''"Ligue du droit international des femmes"'' / LDIF), she has tackled on the international level the fashion for invoking of "[[cultural relativism]]" as a justification for opposing the universal application of women's rights.<ref name=ASselonLDIF>{{cite web |title=Qui est la présidente de la LDIF? |url=http://www.ldif.asso.fr/?theme=ldif&n=354 |work=Autour de la Ligue |publisher=La Ligue du Droit International des Femmes, Paris |access-date=29 January 2021}}</ref>   She has also taken a lead in combatting violence against young girls with immigrant backgrounds:  issues on which she has campaigned include [[Female genital mutilation|excision]], [[Expatriate|forced expatriation]] and various classes of [[Honor killing|"honour crime"]].<ref name=ASselonLDIF/>   A particularly high-profile [[cause célèbre]] into which she launched herself became identified by slogan-headline "Mères d’Alger" (''loosely, "Mothers of Algiers"''):<ref name=MéresAlgeriennes>{{cite web |url=http://www.ldif.asso.fr/?theme=international&n=35|title=Les Méres d'Alger|work=Actualité internationale |publisher=La Ligue du Droit International des Femmes, Paris |access-date=29 January 2021}}</ref>   A shared [[French Algeria|colonial history]] had left several hundred thousand [[Algerians in France]], many of whom came from families that had [[Évian Accords|ended]] the [[Algerian War]] on the "wrong" side.   During the 1980s a succession of cases came to the fore in which, following marital ructions, fathers with Algerian connections had removed their children to [[Algeria]], in defiance of French court rulings granting custody of the children in question to their mothers remaining in France.   In an effort to provide a remedy for these cases, in August 1986 the governments of [[France]] and [[Algeria]] signed a convention,{{efn  |"décret J.O du 19.08.1986"}} but a view quickly emerged that this had failed to provide an effective remedy.   Under Sugier's leadership, the LDIF played a major role in highlighting the issues.   A particular atrocity in point was the [[Killing of Sohane Benziane|"Sohane affair"]], which came up in 2002.<ref name=ASselonLDIF/>{{efn |On October 4, 2002 in [[Vitry-sur-Seine]], 17-year-old Sohane Benziane was burned alive in front of her friends in a cellar by her former boyfriend, a local gang leader.<ref name=AffaireSohane>{{cite web|url=http://www.mariebrenner.com/articles/daughters/daughters.html|title=Daughters of France, Daughters of Allah |author=Marie Brenner |work=From news reports, it may have seemed that the greatest threat to France's secular values was Islamic headscarves in public schools. But thousands of the French girls wearing the scarf are trapped in strict Muslim families, forced into marriage, and brutalized for seeking the freedoms all around them. |year=2004 |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20051123230346/http://www.mariebrenner.com/articles/daughters/daughters.html |access-date=29 January 2021|archive-date=2005-11-23 }}</ref>}}   The LDIF received an appeal from the murdered girl's father and sisters that it should join itself as a civil party to the ensuing legal case against the murder suspect and his accomplice, in order "to support the struggle for the memory of Sohane and to ensure that the same thing should not happen in the future to any other person".<ref name=ChronologieprocédureSohane>{{cite web|url=http://www.ldif.asso.fr/pdf/une/SohaneChrono.pdf|title=Sohane Benziane: Fiche présentant la chronologie des faits, de la procédure judiciaire et des actions de solidarité |publisher=La Ligue du Droit International des Femmes, Paris |access-date=29 January 2021}}</ref>   The trial evidently took some time to prepare, but when it was held, between 31 March and 7 April 2007, the killer and his accomplice were both found guilty.   The killer received a 25-year jail sentence while the accomplice was sentenced to 8 years.   The accomplice now made the tactical error of lodging an appeal.   The LDIF legal team seized the opportunity and lodged their own appeal.   The LDIF was represented at the trial by [[Linda Weil-Curiel]], a lawyer with a reputation in the field of women's rights:   Sugier and Weil-Curiel had made their important first visit to the dead girl's sister and father together.   Throughout the trial Weil-Cureil had emphasized the sexist aspect of the case, and the [[:fr:Avocat général (France)|advocate general]] clearly took full cognisance of her submissions.   The LDIF was represented not in respect of the criminal aspects of the matter but as a civil litigant:  on 18 September 2006 the court responsible for the civil aspect of the case accepted that the LDIF intervention was "admissible and well founded".   The appeal in respect of the accomplice was heard at the [[Seine-Saint-Denis]] [[Cour d'assises#Appellate Assize Court|Court of Assizes]] between 8 June and 14 June 2007; a ten-year jail term was substituted for the earlier, lesser sentence.<ref name= ChronologieprocédureSohane/><ref name=PlaqueErrante>{{cite web|author=Annie Sugier|url=http://www.ldif.asso.fr/pdf/ldif/AS_temps_modernes.pdf |date=20 February 2008|title=La Plaque Errante|publisher=[[Les Temps modernes]], [[Paris]] |pages=1–11 |access-date= 30 January 2021}}</ref>   After the verdict, Annie Sugier produced a rapid succession of statements and articles celebrating the fact that for the first time, under pressure from the LIDF's involvement in the case, [[:fr:Organisation juridictionnelle (France)|a court in France]] had been persuaded to respond to the acts of torture and barbarism of which Sohane Benziane was the victim, to acknowledge the concept of "a sexist crime".<ref name=Cheminscroisés>{{cite web |url=http://www.ldif.asso.fr/pdf/ldif/34-4-Sugier_Beauvoir.pdf |pages=302–307 |work= Testimonios de Annie Sugier, Presidenta de la Liga del Derecho Internacional de las Mujeres |title=Nos chemins se sont croisés |author1= Annie Sugier |author2=Kahina Benziane |publisher=La Ligue du Droit International des Femmes, Paris |access-date=30 January 2021}}</ref>

Annie Sugier is a member of the [[Socialist Party (France)|Socialist Party]].<ref name=ASselonArchivesUA>{{cite web |pages= 52–53 |title=Sugier Annie –48 AF: Présentation du contenu: .... Historique du producteur  |work=Centre d'Archives du féminisme (CAF) |date=2020 |url=https://bu.univ-angers.fr/sites/default/files/Etat_des_fds_feministes.pdf |publisher=[[University of Angers|Université d'Angers]] (Bibliothèque et Archives) |access-date=30 January 2021}}</ref>  She regularly contributes to [[Libération]], [[Le Monde]], and the political journal [[Riposte Laïque]].<ref name="BeitraegezuLib">{{cite web |title=Tous les articles de Annie Sugier publiés dans Libération. |url=https://www.liberation.fr/auteur/9225-annie-sugier |access-date=30 January 2021 |publisher=[[Libération]], Paris}}</ref><ref name="ASTribune09jan2021" />  Sugier quit the Riposte editorial team during the summer of 2010, indicating that she no longer found herself in agreement with its tone and political alliances.<ref name=UmWuerstchen>{{cite web |url=https://ripostelaique.com/Les-mot-d-ordre-des-adversaires-de.html |author=Annie Sugier |date=14 June 2010 |title=Les mot d'ordre des adversaires de l'apéro : courage fuyons ! |publisher=[[Riposte Laïque]], [[:fr:Saint-Jean-d'Acre|"Saint-Jean-d'Acre"]] |access-date=30 January 2021}}</ref> She formally broke with the Riposte Laïque movement in 2012.<ref name=ASquitteRiposte2012>{{cite web|title=La Riposte laïque qui voulait se faire aussi grosse que Pegida |url= https://lahorde.samizdat.net/la-riposte-laique-qui-voulait-se-faire-aussi-grosse-que-pegida|date= 15 January 2015|work=La Horde |publisher=[[:fr:Réseau d'étude, de formation et de lutte contre l'extrême droite et la xénophobie|Réseau d'étude, de formation et de lutte contre l'extrême droite et la xénophobie]]|access-date=31 January 2021}}</ref>

The best known of Annie Sugier's other feminist campaigns involves sport:  more specifically the [[Olympic Games]].   In 1995 she joined with others to set up the so-called "Atlanta+ Committee", in order to draw attention to and denounce sexual apartheid and discrimination against sportswomen more broadly.<ref name=ASiGmAP>{{cite web |author=Ana Pak |date=June 2012 |title=À la Rencontre d'Annie Sugier |work=Échange autour de son livre Femmes voilées aux Jeux Olympiques (ou Les femmes courent-elles moins vite que les Noirs ?) |publisher=Femmes sous lois musulmanes, Londres |url=http://www.wluml.org/fr/news/%C3%A0-la-rencontre-dannie-sugier |access-date=30 January 2021}}</ref>   In 2012 she published "Femmes voilées aux Jeux olympiques" (''"Veiled Women at the Olympic Games"'') which covered more than twenty years of "Atlanta+ Committee" campaigning.<ref name="Femmesvoilees">{{cite book |last1=Sugier |first1=Annie |url=https://www.decitre.fr/livres/femmes-voilees-aux-jeux-olympiques-9782874661969.html |title=Femmes voilées aux Jeux olympiques |last2=Lizin |first2=Anne-Marie |last3=Weil-Curiel |first3=Linda |date=9 April 2012 |publisher=Jourdan Editions |isbn=978-2-87466-196-9 |access-date=30 January 2021}}</ref>   Timed to coincide with the [[2012 Summer Olympics]], "Londres 2012: Justice pour les femmes" (''"London 2012: Justice for the women"'') was published under her direction and that of Linda Weil-Curiel.   That was followed four years later by "Appliquez la Charte olympique" (''"Follow the Olympic Charter"''), timed to coincide with the [[2016 Summer Olympics]].   The campaigning continues in respect of the [[2024 Summer Olympics]] scheduled for [[Paris]].<ref name=ASperJD>{{cite web|title=French feminist group call for hijab ban at Paris 2024|author=James Diamond |date=4 February 2019|publisher=Dunsar Media Company Limited ("Inside the games"), [[Milton Keynes]]|url=https://www.insidethegames.biz/articles/1075127/french-feminist-group-call-for-hijab-ban-at-paris-2024|access-date=30 January 2021}}</ref>

Annie Sugier was a jury member for the [[Simone de Beauvoir Prize |Simone de Beauvoir Prize for Women's Liberation]].<ref name=ProxsdB>{{cite web |title=Le Prix " Simone de Beauvoir pour la liberté des femmes " créé sur l'initiative de Julia Kristeva |url=http://www.kristeva.fr/prixBeauvoir.html |publisher=[[Julia Kristeva]] |access-date=31 January 2021}}</ref>   She is a member of the [[:fr:Coordination française pour le lobby européen des femmes  |"French co-ordination [organisation] for the European Women's Lobby" (''"Coordination française pour le lobby européen des femmes"''/ CLEF)]] and of the "Movement for Peace and against Terrorism" (''"Mouvement pour la paix et contre le terrorisme"'' / MPCT).<ref name=ASselonLDIF/>   She gave evidence before the 2003 [[National Assembly (France)|parliamentary]] enquiry into the contentious issues surrounding the wearing of religious symbols in schools the 2010 enquiry on the wearing if a full veil.<ref name=ASetIEJ>{{cite journal |title=L'universalité des droits se décline-t-elle au féminin? |author=Annie Sugier |journal=Observatoire de la Société Britannique |pages=241–256 |date=2012 |issue=13 |url=https://journals.openedition.org/osb/1483?lang=en |publisher=[[:fr:Centre pour l'Édition Électronique Ouverte|Open Edition Journals]] |doi=10.4000/osb.1483 |access-date=31 January 2021|url-access=subscription }}</ref> Both enquiries were followed by substantive pieces of legislation.<ref name=ASetIEJ/>   She has also testified before [[Senate (France)|senate]] committees on women's rights, equality of life opportunities between genders and gender equality in sport.<ref name=RappSenaEgalité>{{cite web|title=Egalité des femmes et des hommes dans le sport: comme dans le marathon, ce sont les derniers mètres les plus difficiles|work=Rapport d'information n° 650 (2010-2011) de Mme Michèle ANDRÉ, fait au nom de la délégation aux droits des femmes|date=21 June 2011|publisher=Sénat (Rapports d'information), Paris|url=http://www.senat.fr/rap/r10-650/r10-6501.pdf|access-date=31 January 2021}}</ref>
